title: Runtime operator-variant catalogue curation and adaptive selection
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a compact, searchable catalogue of operator variants (attention implementations, matmul kernels, fused operator paths) and build a lightweight runtime advisor that picks the best variant per-request using architecture fingerprint + sequence-length heuristics.

Background: We observe wide per-request variation across sequence-length distributions and GPU topology. Existing hardwired selection rules are brittle for mixed workloads and cause 8-25% tail latency regressions in experimental traces. This work aims to centralize variant metadata, canonicalize performance fingerprints, and wire an adaptive selection policy into the runtime decoding pipeline with fast fallbacks.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduced median and p95 token latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads by >= 10% on test clusters (A100 + H100 mix).
- Fall-back correctness: no increase in generation errors after variant switch (end-to-end QA pass).
- Catalogue API and metadata standardized; at least 12 operator variants profiled and onboarded.
- Runtime advisor must make selection decision in <= 150 microseconds per request (excl. profiling warmups).

Design summary:
1) Variant catalogue: a small JSONL store containing entries with: variant_id, op_family, hardware_tags, seq_len_bucket_range, memory_profile, stability_score, perf_samples_link. We'll centralize format and embed a short provenance string (PR/bench job).
2) Profiler jobs: lightweight microbench harness (GitHub actions jobs + k8s batch) that emits per-variant latency/cost distributions across seq-len buckets and tight QoS budgets.
3) Runtime advisor: a pluggable policy that consumes request fingerprint (gpu_arch, free_memory, prefer_latency/throughput, seq_len_estimate, prefills) and looks up top-k variants. It will use a small heuristic cost function combining observed p50/p95, stability_score, and an adaptive exploration epsilon.
4) Safety & fallback: a fast rollback path that switches to a baseline variant when latency or error rate drifts beyond thresholds within a sliding window.

Implementation plan:
- Week 0: Schema and catalogue format (this ticket). Confluence spec + example entries.
- Week 1: Microbench harness + perf job templates. Start profiling 6 candidate variants.
- Week 2: Runtime advisor prototype in the decoder hot path behind a feature flag. Add telemetry hooks.
- Week 3: Canary in dedicated testing cluster; A/B evaluation vs baseline for 72h.
- Week 4: Analysis and rollout (adjust epsilon, guardrails).

Telemetry and observability:
- New telemetry events: variant_select decision (variant_id, reason, score), fallback_event (from_variant,to_variant,trigger_reason), variant_perf_sample (seq_bucket,latency_ms,success).
- Dashboards: per-variant latency/cost curves, selection frequency heatmaps by seq-len and model, rollback count. Use existing dashboard template: https://dashboards.redwood.com/runtime/variant-selection

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for catalogue parsing and cost function (CI).
- Integration test harness that replays prefill+decode traces and asserts no regressions vs baseline for quality and latency.
- Canary run with synthetic mixed traffic and an internal canary tenant.

Rollout and guardrails:
- Feature-flag gated. Start with 5% of traffic on dedicated cluster.
- Auto-disable if p95 latency increases by >5% or error_rate increases by >1% absolute for 15m.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: profiler noise on shared clusters. Mitigation: use reserved microbench nodes for initial profiling; store stability_score to downweight noisy variants.
- Risk: variant selection adds CPU overhead in hot path. Mitigation: keep lookup path O(1) with precomputed candidate lists and tiny inlined cost fn.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Operator+Variant+Catalogue
- Benchmark job template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-bench/actions/workflows/variant-bench.yml
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1478
- Dashboard (canary): https://dashboards.redwood.com/runtime/variant-canary-457001

Next milestones:
- M1 (schema + 6 variants profiled) by 2026-03-05 (blocked briefly by infra quota).
- M2 (runtime advisor behind flag + telemetry) by 2026-03-15.
- M3 (stable canary with rollback tuning) by 2026-03-29.
